title: VPC after-deploy warmup probes and smoke harness
creator: Maya Patel
description: Add a lightweight, repeatable after-deploy probe suite that runs automatically after Terraform apply for Private (VPC) deployments. The suite will validate API readiness, perform a model warm-up/load check for at least one pinned model variant, and execute a small set of smoke generation and embedding checks. The goal is to catch common post-deploy failures (auth config, networking, model artifacts not present, runtime OOMs, kernel selection failures) before marking a rollout as successful.
acceptance_criteria: A GitHub Actions job (private-deploy/probes) can be triggered by post-apply hook and returns non-zero on failure
Healthcheck endpoint validation: /health, /ready, and token-auth flow tested (200 + expected JSON schema)
Model load check completes: model loads within 90s and responds to a basic generate call with expected token output
Smoke generation: 3 short prompts (seq len 16/128/512) succeed with p95 latency < 2.5s on dedicated small instance profile
Embedding smoke: sample text yields embedding vector length matching model spec and cosine similarity sanity check passes
Automatic retry/backoff on transient errors (3 attempts) and clear failure diagnostics written to a post-deploy artifact bucket
Post-deploy probe logs and metrics are available in Console under deployment -> probes with token-level breakdown and a one-click rerun
Terraform module linkages: probes can be toggled via module variable enable_postdeploy_probes = true and respect lifecycle policies
test_plan: Create a disposable VPC deployment via terraform/apply in staging with enable_postdeploy_probes=true
Run GH Actions job private-deploy/probes against the new control plane endpoint; capture stdout/stderr to artifact store
Verify the model warmup uses the same bootstrap path as runtime (artifact path) to avoid false positives
Intentionally break a config (bad IAM role or missing model file) to verify probe fails and surfaces meaningful error strings
Measure probe run time and resource usage; ensure it completes under 5 minutes for typical small deployments
implementation_notes: Will reuse existing runtime health endpoints; add a small wrapper that exercises streaming and non-streaming code paths
Model warmup will use the same caching API as production path to ensure KV cache and tokenizer initialization occur
Prefer k8s Job triggered by postapply webhook for customers using on-prem; fallback to GH Actions for hosted CI runs
Artifacts written to s3://redwood-postdeploy-probes/<deployment-id>/ for later debugging; link exposed in Console
Avoid loading large models for the default probe; use a configurable probe_model variable (default: small-vert) per deployment
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Probe itself could increase deploy time. Mitigation: default to lightweight profile and cap at 5 minutes; make opt-in via terraform boolean
Risk: Probes may introduce additional permissions (list/read model artifacts). Mitigation: document least-privilege IAM requirements and add an RBAC test in the probe
Risk: False negatives due to cold-start variance. Mitigation: allow 3 retries with exponential backoff and report median + max timings
Risk: Cost impact when running probes for many customers. Mitigation: probe frequency is configurable (once-per-deploy by default) and can be disabled for low-cost tiers
